title: How To Create An Exploding Garment Animation In Clo
description:
In this tutorial, you will learn how to seamlessly animate your garments from one state to another using the Morph Target tool in CLO. We also cover how to create a smooth turntable animation using Key Frames.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
0:38 How to save your OBJ Garments
4:16 Avatar Morph
6:43 Animation Mode
7:19 Key Frame Animation

IMPORTANT : As of 2024.2 you must have Seam Face Turned On in the Property Editor for Pattern Pieces : Pattern Piece Property Editor - Geometry - Extrusion Direction

markdown_content: ## Introduction to Morph Target Animation in Clo 3D This section introduces the concept of using Morph Target in Clo 3D to animate a garment transitioning between two states, such as a sewn state and an exploded view. It covers the initial setup by opening an existing garment file and preparing it for export. - Open an existing garment project in Clo 3D (example: a blazer from the Clo Connect store). - The workspace consists of a 3D window and a 2D pattern window. - To prepare for morph target animation, export the garment’s pattern pieces as an OBJ file. - Select all pattern pieces and use **File > Export > OBJ Selected**. - Save files using descriptive names indicating the garment’s state (e.g., “demo sewn” for the sewn state). - In the export options: - Choose **Selected Patterns**. - Select **All Graphics and Trims** to include details like button trims. - Set the surface to **Thick** for textured surfaces. - Use **Absolute Textures** for accurate texture mapping. - Export the sewn garment state as an OBJ file. --- ## Creating and Exporting the Second Garment State (Exploded View) This section explains saving the garment in a different state to create the morph target transition, such as an exploded or apart view, by adjusting pattern pieces and exporting again. - Use **File > Save As** to create a new project file for the second garment state (e.g., “Blazer Apart View”). - Modify pattern pieces to reflect the new state: - Reset pieces to 2D flat state or move them apart manually. - Utilize avatar’s arrangement points if needed. - Once the second state is set, export all pattern pieces again using the same export process: - **File > Export > OBJ Selected**. - Name this export appropriately (e.g., “demo apart”). - Maintain the same export settings as the sewn state (Selected Patterns, Graphics and Trims, Thick surface, Absolute Textures). - This process results in two OBJ files representing different garment states for morphing. --- ## Setting Up a Clean Workspace and Importing OBJ Files This section covers starting fresh with a new Clo 3D project to begin the morph target animation setup and importing the exported OBJ files representing different garment states. - Open a new Clo 3D project via **File > New Project** for a clean workspace. - Hide the 2D window to maximize screen space by clicking on the 3D view button. - Import the OBJ file for the starting garment state (e.g., exploded view): - Use the linked folder panel to add and open the OBJ file. - Double-click or right-click to open; ensure the correct OBJ (apart view) is loaded. - If the wrong OBJ is opened, delete it and import the correct one. Clo 3D allows easy correction without penalty. - The imported OBJ represents the garment as a solid object with individual pattern pieces visually separated. --- ## Using Morph Target to Animate Between Garment States This section details how to use Clo 3D’s Morph Target feature to create an animation that transitions the garment from one state (exploded) to another (sewn). - Open the **Morph Target** tool in Clo 3D. - Instead of double-clicking the second state OBJ to add it, right-click and select **Add to Workspace**. - Change the object type from **Avatar** to **Morph Target** to enable morphing functionality. - Clo 3D processes the morph target by calculating the transformation between the two states. - Access animation mode by switching from **Simulation** to **Animation**. - Use the animation bar to scrub through frames and preview the garment morphing from exploded to sewn state. - The morph target animation is automatically generated once both OBJ states are loaded. --- ## Adding Camera Motion Using Keyframes This section explains how to enhance the morph target animation by adding dynamic camera movements using keyframes introduced in Clo 3D version 7. - In animation mode, add keyframes to control camera position and rotation. - Open the camera viewfinder to see the camera’s perspective and path. - To create a rotating camera effect around the garment: - Set a keyframe at the starting frame (e.g., frame 0) with camera rotation Y at 0 degrees. - Set another keyframe at the ending frame (e.g., frame 30) with camera rotation Y at 360 degrees. - Playing the animation will show the camera circling the garment as it morphs, creating a 360-degree turntable effect. - Adjust camera settings such as position, focus point, and line of sight within the camera group controls. - Keyframes enable smooth transitions and can be combined with other animation elements. --- ## Final Rendering and Export This section summarizes how to prepare the completed morph target animation with camera motion for rendering. - After setting up the morph target animation and camera keyframes: - Switch to the render engine in Clo 3D. - Add lighting and other visual effects as desired. - Render the final video of the garment morphing with the animated camera. - The result is a professional turntable animation showcasing the garment transitioning between states. - Example finished videos demonstrate the effectiveness of this workflow in presenting garment designs dynamically. --- # Summary This tutorial covers the complete workflow in Clo 3D to create an exploding garment animation using Morph Target. Key steps include exporting garment states as OBJ files, importing them into a new project, applying morph target animation to transition between states, and enhancing the presentation with camera keyframe animations. The process allows designers to visualize garments dynamically and produce engaging turntable animations for presentations or portfolios.
